sections.overview: Phyllotis osgoodi is a poorly known Andean sigmodontine rodent recorded from northern Chile.
sections.identification: Its species status has been questioned because researchers found no clear morphological distinction from sympatric Phyllotis xanthopygus.
sections.habitat: The modern mammal synthesis knows it only from its type locality in the Puna of northern Chile.
sections.diet: No field data on its diet were available in the detailed mammal synthesis consulted.
sections.behavior: Its behaviour in the wild has not been studied in the sources consulted.
sections.reproduction: The field biology account does not report species-specific reproductive information.
sections.ecology: An older Chilean museum account placed it in the puna at about four thousand four hundred metres; its limits and range remain uncertain.
sections.conservation: Mammal Diversity Database lists it as Not Evaluated; this should not be read as evidence of low risk.
